title.zh: 卷一百六十六 列傳第五十三: 王綧 隋世昌 羅璧 劉恩 石高山 鞏彥暉 蔡珍 張泰亨 賀祉 孟德子義 鄭義 張榮實 石抹狗狗 楚鼎 樊楫 張均 信苴日 王昔剌 趙宏偉
title.en: Volume 166 Biographies 53: Wang Zhun, Sui Shichang, Luo Bi, Liu En, Shi Gaoshan, Gong Yanhui, Cai Zhen, Zhang Taiheng, He Zhi, Meng Deziyi, Zheng Yi, Zhang Rongshi, Shi Mogougou, Chu Ding, Fan Ji, Zhang Jun, Xin Juri, Wang Xila, Zhao Hongwei
title.raw: 卷一百六十六 列傳第五十三: 王綧 隋世昌 羅璧 劉恩 石高山 鞏彥暉 蔡珍 張泰亨 賀祉 孟德子義 鄭義 張榮實 石抹狗狗 楚鼎 樊楫 張均 信苴日 王昔剌 趙宏偉 Volume 166 Biographies 53: Wang Zhun, Sui Shichang, Luo Bi, Liu En, Shi Gaoshan, Gong Yanhui, Cai Zhen, Zhang Taiheng, He Zhi, Meng Deziyi, Zheng Yi, Zhang Rongshi, Shi Mogougou, Chu Ding, Fan Ji, Zhang Jun, Xin Juri, Wang Xila, Zhao Hongwei

sentences.zh: 王綧，高麗王之猶子也，美容儀，慷慨有志略，善騎射，讀書通大義，以質子入朝。

translations.literal: Wang Zhun was a nephew of the King of Goryeo; he had a handsome bearing, was generous and possessed strategic vision, excelled at riding and archery, read books and understood great principles, and entered court as a hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhun, a nephew of the King of Goryeo, was handsome and openhanded, with both strategic vision and skill in riding and archery. He read widely and grasped the larger moral principles, and came to court as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 歲癸丑，高麗權臣高令公叛，憲宗命耶虎大王東征，綧奉旨為使講和，仍鎮守其地，時高麗人戶新附者，就命綧總之。

translations.literal: In the year guichou, Goryeo's powerful minister Gao Lingong rebelled; Emperor Xianzong ordered Prince Ye Hu to campaign east. Zhun received orders as envoy to negotiate peace and still garrisoned the region; at that time the newly submitted Goryeo households were placed under Zhun's overall command.
translations.idiomatic: In the guichou year Goryeo's powerful minister Gao Lingong rebelled. Emperor Xianzong sent Prince Ye Hu east on campaign, and Zhun was ordered to serve as envoy to negotiate peace while continuing to hold the region. Newly submitted Goryeo households were placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，授金符總管，升佩虎符，兼領軍民。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, he was appointed Supervisor with a gold tally; he was promoted to wear the tiger tally and concurrently commanded both army and people.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong (1260) he was made supervisor with a gold tally, then promoted to the tiger tally and given joint charge of troops and civilians.

sentences.zh: 三年，率兵徵濟南李璮。

translations.literal: In the third year, he led troops to campaign against Li Tan of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he led troops against Li Tan of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 至元七年，高麗臣林衍叛，世祖遣頭輦哥國王討之，綧簽領部民一千三百戶，與國王同行。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan, the Goryeo subject Lin Yan rebelled; the Founder sent Prince Tounaige to suppress him. Zhun signed on to lead thirteen hundred households of his tribesmen and went with the prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan (1270) the Goryeo subject Lin Yan rebelled. Kublai sent Prince Tounaige to suppress him, and Zhun took command of thirteen hundred households of his followers and marched with the prince.

sentences.zh: 是年十一月，以疾辭還，家居。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year, he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home to live in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: That November he resigned for illness and returned home to live in retirement.

sentences.zh: 二十年九月，卒，壽六十一。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twentieth year, he died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of the twentieth year, at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 子三人。

translations.literal: He had three sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons.

sentences.zh: 阿剌帖木兒襲職，授虎符，總管高麗人戶。

translations.literal: Alatietie'er succeeded to the office, was granted the tiger tally, and served as supervisor of Goryeo households.
translations.idiomatic: Alatietie'er inherited the post, received the tiger tally, and became supervisor of Goryeo households.

sentences.zh: 至元八年，將兵討叛賊金通精，賊敗走耽羅。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan, he led troops to suppress the rebel Jin Tongjing; the rebels were defeated and fled to Tamna.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan (1271) he led troops against the rebel Jin Tongjing. The rebels were beaten and fled to Tamna.

sentences.zh: 十一年，進昭勇大將軍，從都元帥忽都徵日本國，預有戰功。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he was promoted to General of Manifest Courage and followed Grand Marshal Hudu on the campaign against Japan, sharing in the military achievements.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to general of manifest courage and followed Grand Marshal Hudu against Japan, earning a share of the campaign's credit.

sentences.zh: 十五年，加鎮國上將軍、安撫使、高麗軍民總管，尋升輔國上將軍、東征左副都元帥。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he was additionally made General Who Stabilizes the State, Pacification Commissioner, and Supervisor of Goryeo Army and People; soon after he was promoted to General Who Assists the State and Left Deputy Grand Marshal of the Eastern Expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was also made a stabilizing-state general, pacification commissioner, and supervisor of Goryeo military and civilians, and soon after was promoted to assisting-state general and left deputy grand marshal of the eastern expedition.

sentences.zh: 十八年，复徵日本，遇風濤，遂沒於軍。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he again campaigned against Japan; encountering wind and waves, he perished with the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he campaigned against Japan again, but was lost with his army in a storm.

sentences.zh: 闊闊帖木兒，入侍武宗潛邸，積勞授太中大夫、管民總管。

translations.literal: Kuokuotiemie'er entered service at Emperor Wuzong's princely residence; for accumulated merit he was appointed Grand Master of Palace Counsel and Supervisor of the People.
translations.idiomatic: Kuokuotiemie'er served at Emperor Wuzong's household before his accession; for long service he was made grand master of palace counsel and supervisor of the people.

sentences.zh: 兀愛，襲兄阿刺帖木兒職，佩金虎符，授安遠大將軍、安撫使、高麗軍民總管、東征左副都元帥。

translations.literal: Wu Ai succeeded to his elder brother Alatietie'er's office, wore the gold tiger tally, and was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant, Pacification Commissioner, Supervisor of Goryeo Army and People, and Left Deputy Grand Marshal of the Eastern Expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ai inherited his brother Alatietie'er's post, wore the gold tiger tally, and was made a pacifying-the-distant general, pacification commissioner, supervisor of Goryeo military and civilians, and left deputy grand marshal of the eastern expedition.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，乃顏叛，力戰屢捷。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, Nayan rebelled; he fought fiercely and won repeated victories.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, when Nayan rebelled, he fought hard and won battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 復從月魯兒那演討塔不歹、朵歡大王於蒙可山、那江，統兵五千餘眾，與八剌哈赤脫歡相拒，絕流戰黑龍江，箭中右臂，忍傷复戰，敵大敗。

translations.literal: He again followed Yuelu'ernayan to campaign against Princes Tabudai and Duohuan at Mengke Mountain and the Najiang, commanding more than five thousand troops. He opposed Balaqachi Tuhuan, fought across the current on the Amur, was struck in the right arm by an arrow, endured the wound and fought on again, and the enemy was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Yuelu'ernayan against Princes Tabudai and Duohuan at Mengke Mountain and the Najiang, leading more than five thousand men. Opposing Balaqachi Tuhuan, he fought across the Amur, took an arrow in his right arm, pressed on despite the wound, and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，徵哈丹禿魯幹，隸平章闊裡帖木兒麾下，論功居多。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, he campaigned against Hadan Tulugan, served under Pingzhang Kuolitiemie'er, and in the reckoning of merit ranked foremost.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he campaigned against Hadan Tulugan under Pingzhang Kuolitiemie'er and ranked at the top when merits were assessed.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月，賊軍古都禿魯幹次於斡禿魯塞，平章率兀愛討降之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter, the rebel army of Gudu Tulugan encamped at Wotuluse; the Pingzhang led Wu Ai to campaign and accept their surrender.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in the twelfth month, the rebel Gudu Tulugan's force encamped at Wotuluse. The pingzhang led Wu Ai to attack and accept their surrender.

sentences.zh: 明年，加授昭武大將軍、遼陽等處行中書省事。

translations.literal: The next year, he was additionally appointed General of Manifest Martiality and charged with the affairs of the Branch Secretariat of Liaoyang and other regions.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was also made a manifest-martiality general and put in charge of the Liaoyang regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: 又明年，哈丹等入寇高麗國境，遣兀愛鎮守，仍修城壁，嚴卒伍，軍威大振，賊遂潛遁。

translations.literal: The year after that, Hadan and others invaded Goryeo's borders; Wu Ai was sent to garrison the region, still repaired the walls, tightened the ranks, and the army's prestige greatly rose, whereupon the rebels secretly fled.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Hadan and others raided Goryeo. Wu Ai was sent to hold the frontier, repair the walls, and drill the ranks until army morale soared and the raiders slipped away.

sentences.zh: 九月，哈丹禿魯幹復寇纏春，兀愛引兵擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Hadan Tulugan again raided Chanchun; Wu Ai led troops and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Hadan Tulugan raided Chanchun again; Wu Ai led troops and beat him back.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，入覲世祖於內殿，嘉其戰功，賜尚方玉帶及銀酒器。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, he entered the inner hall to pay homage to the Founder; the Founder praised his military achievements and bestowed an imperial jade belt and silver wine vessels.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was received by Kublai in the inner hall. The emperor praised his battlefield record and gave him an imperial jade belt and silver wine vessels.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，改東征左副都元帥府，立總管高麗女直漢軍萬戶府，乃授兀愛三珠虎符，升鎮國上將軍，總管高麗女直漢軍萬戶府，兼瀋陽安撫使、高麗軍民總管。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, the Left Deputy Grand Marshal's Office of the Eastern Expedition was reorganized and the Ten-thousand-household Office of Goryeo, Jurchen, and Han Troops was established; Wu Ai was then granted the three-pearl tiger tally, promoted to General Who Stabilizes the State, made supervisor of the Goryeo-Jurchen-Han ten-thousand-household office, and concurrently made Pacification Commissioner of Shenyang and Supervisor of Goryeo Army and People.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year the eastern expedition's left deputy marshal's office was reorganized and a ten-thousand-household office for Goryeo, Jurchen, and Han troops was created. Wu Ai received the three-pearl tiger tally, was promoted to stabilizing-state general, made head of that office, and also served as Shenyang pacification commissioner and supervisor of Goryeo military and civilians.

sentences.zh: ○隋世昌

translations.literal: ○ Sui Shichang
translations.idiomatic: Sui Shichang

sentences.zh: 隋世昌，其先登州棲霞人。

translations.literal: Sui Shichang: his ancestors were people of Qixia in Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Shichang's family came from Qixia in Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 父寶，徙居萊陽，金末隸軍伍，主帥奇其貌，以為管軍謀克，俄授懷遠大將軍、管軍都總領，鎮行村海口。

translations.literal: His father Bao moved to live in Laiyang; at the end of the Jin he entered military service. The commander-in-chief marveled at his appearance and made him a military planning officer (mouke); soon he was appointed General Who Cherishes the Distant and Commander-in-Chief of the Army, garrisoning Xingcun Haikou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bao moved to Laiyang and entered the army at the end of the Jin. The commander was struck by his looks and made him a military planning officer; soon he was made a cherishing-the-distant general and army commander-in-chief, stationed at Xingcun Haikou.

sentences.zh: 太宗下山東，寶遂來歸，授萊陽令，歷萊州節度判官，終高密令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong descended on Shandong, Bao then came over in submission, was appointed magistrate of Laiyang, served as military commissioner of Laizhou, and ended as magistrate of Gaomi.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took Shandong, Bao submitted and was made magistrate of Laiyang, later served as Laizhou military commissioner, and ended his career as magistrate of Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 世昌其第四子也，涉獵書史，善騎射，身長八尺，鍛渾鐵為槍，重四十餘斤，能左右擊刺。

translations.literal: Shichang was his fourth son; he ranged through books and histories, excelled at riding and archery, stood eight feet tall, forged a spear of wrought iron weighing more than forty jin, and could strike and thrust with either hand.
translations.idiomatic: Shichang was his fourth son. He read widely in history, rode and shot well, stood eight feet tall, forged a wrought-iron spear of more than forty jin, and could fight with it in either hand.

sentences.zh: 歲癸丑，選充隊長。

translations.literal: In the year guichou, he was selected to serve as squad leader.
translations.idiomatic: In the guichou year he was chosen as squad leader.

sentences.zh: 宋兵來攻海州，世昌戰卻之。

translations.literal: Song troops came to attack Haizhou; Shichang fought and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When Song forces attacked Haizhou, Shichang fought them off.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，克東海，世昌先登，升馬軍隊官。

translations.literal: In the year renxu, Donghai was taken; Shichang was first to scale the wall and was promoted to cavalry squad officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the renxu year Donghai fell; Shichang was first over the wall and was promoted to cavalry squad officer.

sentences.zh: 己未，攻漣水城，世昌樹雲梯攀緣而上，身被數槍，眾從之，遂克其城，升馬軍千戶。

translations.literal: In the year jiwei, they attacked Liancheng; Shichang set up cloud ladders and climbed up, his body taking several spear wounds; the troops followed him and thus took the city; he was promoted to cavalry thousand-household.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiwei year they assaulted Liancheng. Shichang raised scaling ladders and went up first, taking several spear wounds; the men followed and the city fell, and he was made cavalry thousand-household.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，宋將夏貴軍淮南新城，世昌夜乘艨艟抵城下，宋兵出戰，斬首數百級，刺殺其守將二人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, the Song general Xia Gui garrisoned Xincheng in Huainan; Shichang at night took war junks to reach below the city; Song troops came out to fight; he beheaded several hundred and stabbed to death two of their defending generals.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong the Song general Xia Gui held Xincheng in Huainan. Shichang took war junks by night to the foot of the walls; when Song troops came out he killed several hundred men and stabbed two defending generals to death.

sentences.zh: 未幾，漣水復叛歸宋，世昌軍於東馬寨城外，宋兵來攻，世昌擊走之。

translations.literal: Before long Liancheng rebelled again and returned to the Song; Shichang encamped outside Dongmazhai; Song troops came to attack and Shichang struck and drove them away.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liancheng rebelled and went back to the Song. Shichang camped outside Dongmazhai; when Song forces attacked he drove them off.

sentences.zh: 三年，改步軍千戶，還鎮行村海口。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was transferred to infantry thousand-household and returned to garrison Xingcun Haikou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made an infantry thousand-household and returned to garrison Xingcun Haikou.

sentences.zh: 至元元年，朝議分揀正軍奧魯，授萊陽縣諸軍奧魯長官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan, the court deliberated on sorting regular troops and their military households (aolu); he was appointed chief of the military households of all troops in Laiyang County.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhiyuan the court reorganized regular troops and their military households; he was made chief of all such households in Laiyang County.

sentences.zh: 六年，伐宋。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he campaigned against the Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined the campaign against the Song.

sentences.zh: 七年，以世昌為淄萊萬戶府副都鎮撫，守萬山堡，建言修一字城以圍襄、樊，升管軍千戶。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Shichang was made Deputy Pacification Commissioner of the Zilai Ten-thousand-household Office, garrisoned Wanshan Fort, proposed building a single-line wall to besiege Xiangyang and Fancheng, and was promoted to army thousand-household.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made deputy pacification commissioner of the Zilai ten-thousand-household office and held Wanshan Fort. He proposed building a linked wall to besiege Xiangyang and Fancheng and was promoted to army thousand-household.

sentences.zh: 九年，敗宋兵於鹿門山。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he defeated Song troops at Lumen Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he defeated Song forces at Lumen Mountain.

sentences.zh: 元帥劉整築新門，使世昌總其役，樊城出兵來爭，且拒且築，不終夜而就。

translations.literal: Marshal Liu Zheng built the New Gate and had Shichang oversee the work; Fancheng sent troops to contest it; he resisted while building, and before the night was over it was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Marshal Liu Zheng was building the New Gate and put Shichang in charge. Fancheng sent troops to interfere; he fought them off while building, and finished before dawn.

sentences.zh: 整授軍二百，令世昌立砲簾於樊城欄馬牆外，夜大雪，城中矢石如雨，軍校多死傷，達旦而砲簾立。

translations.literal: Liu Zheng gave him two hundred troops and ordered Shichang to erect a gun-screen outside Fancheng's horse-blocking wall; that night heavy snow fell; arrows and stones from the city fell like rain; many officers and soldiers were killed or wounded; by dawn the gun-screen stood.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zheng gave him two hundred men and ordered him to set up a gun-screen outside Fancheng's horse-blocking wall. Snow fell heavily that night while arrows and stones rained from the walls; many of his men were killed or wounded, but by dawn the screen was in place.

sentences.zh: 宋人列艦江上，世昌乘風縱火，燒其船百餘。

translations.literal: The Song lined ships on the river; Shichang took advantage of the wind to set fires and burned more than a hundred of their vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The Song lined ships along the river; Shichang used the wind to set fires and burned more than a hundred vessels.

sentences.zh: 樊城出兵鏖戰欄馬牆下，世昌流血滿甲，勇氣愈壯，而樊城竟破，襄陽亦下，遷武略將軍。

translations.literal: Fancheng sent troops to fight fiercely below the horse-blocking wall; Shichang's armor ran with blood, yet his courage grew stronger; Fancheng was finally taken and Xiangyang also fell; he was transferred to General of Martial Strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Fancheng sent troops to fight below the horse-blocking wall. Shichang's armor was drenched in blood, yet he fought all the harder; Fancheng fell, then Xiangyang, and he was made a martial-strategy general.

sentences.zh: 引兵由黃涴堡入漢江，破沙洋。

translations.literal: He led troops from Huangwan Fort into the Han River and took Shayang.
translations.idiomatic: He led his men from Huangwan Fort into the Han and captured Shayang.

sentences.zh: 攻新城，世昌坎其城而先登，中數矢，傷臂，兜鍪皆裂，昏眩墜地，少蘇復進，遂下新城。

translations.literal: Attacking Xincheng, Shichang undermined the wall and was first to ascend; he was struck by several arrows, wounded in the arm, his helmet split open, fell faint to the ground; after a brief recovery he advanced again and thus took Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: At Xincheng he undermined the wall and went up first. Several arrows struck him, wounding his arm and splitting his helmet; he collapsed in a faint, but after a moment rallied and pressed on until the city fell.

sentences.zh: 明日，丞相伯顏視所坎城，高一丈五尺餘，論功為上。

translations.literal: The next day Chancellor Bayan inspected the undermined wall, more than one zhang and five chi high; in the reckoning of merit he ranked highest.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Chancellor Bayan inspected the breach Shichang had dug, more than fifteen feet high, and ranked his merit first.

sentences.zh: 從諸軍渡江，抵南岸，宋兵聯舟來拒，世昌舍舟師，率蒙古哈必赤軍步戰，斬其將一人，宋師潰，世昌追之，復與戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: Following the armies across the river to the south bank, Song troops linked boats to resist; Shichang left the navy, led Mongol and Qabchiq troops in infantry combat, beheaded one of their generals; the Song army collapsed; Shichang pursued, fought again, and utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed with the main force to the south bank, where Song fleets blocked the way. Shichang left the boats, led Mongol and Qabchiq infantry, and killed a Song general. The Song line broke; he pursued, fought again, and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 十二年，從戰於丁家洲，以功升管軍千戶，佩金符。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he fought at Dingjiazhou; for merit he was promoted to army thousand-household and wore the gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he fought at Dingjiazhou, was promoted to army thousand-household for his service, and received the gold tally.

sentences.zh: 十三年，圍揚州，世昌絕其糧道，兼搜湖泊。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Yangzhou was besieged; Shichang cut off its grain routes and also searched the lakes.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, during the siege of Yangzhou, he cut the grain routes and swept the lakes as well.

sentences.zh: 宋兵聞鐵槍名，不敢近。

translations.literal: Song troops heard the name Iron Spear and did not dare approach.
translations.idiomatic: Song soldiers heard the name Iron Spear and would not come near him.

sentences.zh: 揚州平，充四城兵馬使，從平章阿術入見，授宣武將軍、管軍總管。

translations.literal: When Yangzhou was pacified, he served as military commissioner of the four cities; following Pingzhang A Shu to audience, he was appointed General of Manifest Martiality and Commander of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: After Yangzhou fell he served as military commissioner of the four cities. He followed Pingzhang A Shu to court and was made a manifest-martiality general and army commander.

sentences.zh: 十四年，戍揚州，擊野人原、司空山等七寨，皆下之，進安撫使，佩金虎符，鎮澉浦。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he garrisoned Yangzhou, attacked seven stockades including Yerenyuan and Sikong Mountain, and took them all; he was promoted to Pacification Commissioner, wore the gold tiger tally, and garrisoned Ganpu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he garrisoned Yangzhou and took seven stockades, including Yerenyuan and Sikong Mountain. He was made pacification commissioner, given the gold tiger tally, and stationed at Ganpu.

sentences.zh: 十七年，拜定遠大將軍、管軍萬戶，尋以獲海賊功進階安遠大將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he was appointed General Who Stabilizes the Distant and army ten-thousand-household; soon for capturing pirates he was advanced in rank to General Who Pacifies the Distant.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was made a stabilizing-the-distant general and army ten-thousand-household, and soon after was promoted to pacifying-the-distant general for capturing pirates.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，改沂郯上副萬戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, he was transferred to deputy ten-thousand-household of upper Yitan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was made deputy ten-thousand-household of upper Yitan.

sentences.zh: 世昌前後數百戰，體皆金瘡，竟以是疾卒，年六十一，封定海郡侯，諡忠勇。

translations.literal: Shichang fought several hundred battles before and after; his body bore wounds from metal throughout; he finally died of this illness, aged sixty-one; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dinghai Commandery with the posthumous title Loyal and Brave.
translations.idiomatic: Shichang fought in hundreds of battles and his body was covered with old wounds. He finally died of those injuries at sixty-one. He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dinghai with the posthumous title Loyal and Brave.

sentences.zh: 子國英嗣。

translations.literal: His son Guoying succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guoying succeeded him.

sentences.zh: ○羅璧

translations.literal: ○ Luo Bi
translations.idiomatic: Luo Bi

sentences.zh: 羅璧，字仲玉，鎮江人。

translations.literal: Luo Bi, style name Zhongyu, was a man of Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Bi, styled Zhongyu, was from Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 父大義，為宋將。

translations.literal: His father Dayi was a Song general.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dayi had been a Song general.

sentences.zh: 璧年十三而孤，長從硃蜺孫入蜀，累官武翼大夫、利州西路馬步軍副總管。

translations.literal: Bi was orphaned at thirteen; when grown he followed Zhu Sisun into Shu, and rose through offices to Grand Master of Martial Wings and Deputy Commander of Cavalry and Infantry of Western Lizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Bi lost his father at thirteen. As an adult he followed Zhu Sisun into Sichuan and rose to grand master of martial wings and deputy commander of the cavalry and infantry of western Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 祀孫移荊湖，璧從之，至江陵。

translations.literal: Sisun was transferred to Jinghu; Bi followed him to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Sisun was posted to Jinghu, Bi went with him to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 右丞阿里海牙領軍下江陵，璧從祀孫降，授宣武將軍、管軍千戶，隸丞相阿術麾下。

translations.literal: Right Chancellor Alihaiya led troops down on Jiangling; Bi followed Sisun in surrender, was appointed General of Manifest Martiality and army thousand-household, and was placed under Chancellor Aju.
translations.idiomatic: When Right Chancellor Alihaiya marched on Jiangling, Bi followed Sisun in surrendering. He was made a manifest-martiality general and army thousand-household under Chancellor Aju.

sentences.zh: 招收淮軍，討歙寇有功，領本州安撫事。

translations.literal: He recruited Huai troops; in suppressing bandits in She Prefecture he had merit and took charge of pacification affairs in his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited Huai troops and earned merit suppressing bandits in She Prefecture, then took charge of pacification in his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至元十五年，從元帥張弘範定廣南，賜金符，昇明威將軍、管軍總管，鎮金山。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhiyuan, he followed Marshal Zhang Hongfan in pacifying Guangnan, was granted a gold tally, promoted to General of Bright Martiality and army commander, and garrisoned Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Zhiyuan (1278) he followed Marshal Zhang Hongfan in pacifying Guangnan, received a gold tally, was made a bright-martiality general and army commander, and garrisoned Jinshan.

sentences.zh: 居四年，海盜屏絕。

translations.literal: After four years, pirates were completely eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: After four years pirates had virtually disappeared from the coast.

sentences.zh: 徙鎮上海，督造海舟六十艘，兩月而畢。

translations.literal: He was transferred to garrison Shanghai, supervised the building of sixty seagoing vessels, and finished in two months.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Shanghai, oversaw construction of sixty seagoing ships, and finished in two months.

sentences.zh: 至元十二年，始運江南糧，而河運弗便。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhiyuan, grain transport from Jiangnan began, but river transport was inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Zhiyuan (1275) Jiangnan grain shipments began, but river transport proved impractical.

sentences.zh: 十九年，用丞相伯顏言，初通海道漕運，抵直沽以達京城，立運糧萬戶三，而以璧與硃清、張瑄為之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, following Chancellor Bayan's proposal, the sea-route grain transport was first opened, reaching Zhigu to reach the capital; three grain-transport ten-thousand-household offices were established, with Bi, Zhu Qing, and Zhang Xuan appointed to them.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year (1282), on Chancellor Bayan's advice, the sea route for grain transport was opened to Zhigu and then the capital. Three grain-transport ten-thousand-household offices were created, and Bi, Zhu Qing, and Zhang Xuan were put in charge.

sentences.zh: 乃首部漕舟，由海洋抵楊村，不數十日入京師，賜金虎符，進懷遠大將軍、管軍萬戶，兼管海道運糧。

translations.literal: He then led the first grain convoy, reaching Yangcun by sea in fewer than ten days and entering the capital; he was granted the gold tiger tally, promoted to General Who Cherishes the Distant and army ten-thousand-household, and concurrently directed sea-route grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: He led the first convoy by sea to Yangcun and reached the capital in under ten days. He received the gold tiger tally, was promoted to cherishing-the-distant general and army ten-thousand-household, and also took charge of sea-route grain transport.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，乃顏叛，璧復以漕舟至遼陽​​，浮海抵錦州小凌河，至廣寧十寨，諸軍賴以濟，加昭勇大將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, Nayan rebelled; Bi again took grain ships to Liaoyang, crossed the sea to the Xiaoling River at Jinzhou, reached the ten stockades of Guangning, and the armies relied on this for relief; he was additionally made General of Manifest Courage.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, when Nayan rebelled, Bi again sailed grain ships to Liaoyang, crossed the sea to the Xiaoling River at Jinzhou, and reached the ten stockades at Guangning, supplying the armies when they needed it most. He was made a manifest-courage general.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，督漕至直沽倉，潞河決，水溢，幾及倉，璧樹柵，率所部畚土築堤捍之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, supervising grain transport to the Zhigu granary, the Luo River burst its banks and water overflowed, nearly reaching the granary; Bi set up palisades and led his troops with baskets of earth to build dikes to hold it back.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, while supervising grain shipments to the Zhigu granary, the Luo River burst and floodwater nearly reached the storehouses. Bi threw up palisades and led his men in basket-work to build dikes and hold the water back.

sentences.zh: 升昭毅大將軍、同知淮西道宣慰司事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General of Manifest Resolution and Associate Commissioner of the Huaixi Circuit Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to manifest-resolution general and associate commissioner of the Huaixi pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 請兩淮荒閒之田給貧民耕墾，三年而後量收其入，從之，歲得粟數十萬斛，升鎮國上將軍、海北海南道宣慰使都元帥。

translations.literal: He requested that idle wasteland in the two Huai regions be given to poor people to cultivate; after three years the harvest would be assessed and collected; the request was granted; each year several hundred thousand hu of grain were obtained; he was promoted to General Who Stabilizes the State and Grand Marshal of the Haibei-Hainan Circuit Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that idle land in the two Huai regions be given to the poor to farm, with rent assessed only after three years. The court agreed, and the scheme yielded several hundred thousand hu of grain a year. He was then made stabilizing-state general and grand marshal of the Haibei-Hainan pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 大德三年，除饒州路總管，改廣東道宣慰使都元帥。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dade, he was dismissed as Route Supervisor of Raozhou and made Grand Marshal of the Guangdong Circuit Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dade (1299) he left the Raozhou route supervisor post and became grand marshal of the Guangdong pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 山海獠夷不沾王化，負固反側，乃誘致諸洞蠻夷酋長，假以官位，曉以禍福，由是咸率眾以歸。

translations.literal: Mountain and sea Liao tribes had not received royal transformation and held fast in rebellion; he then invited the chieftains of the various cave barbarians, granted them nominal offices, and explained benefit and harm to them; thereby they all led their followers to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain and coastal tribes had never accepted imperial rule and clung to their strongholds. He summoned chieftains from the cave settlements, offered them nominal offices, and explained the consequences of resistance and submission, until they all brought their people in.

sentences.zh: 除都水監，改正奉大夫。

translations.literal: He was dismissed as Superintendent of Waterways and made Rectifier Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: He was made superintendent of waterways and rectifier grand master.

sentences.zh: 通州復多水患，鑿二渠以分水勢；

translations.literal: Tongzhou again suffered many flood disasters; he dug two canals to divide the water's force;
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhou suffered repeated flooding; he dug two canals to divert the water;

sentences.zh: 又浚阜通河而廣之，歲增漕六十餘萬石。

translations.literal: He also dredged and widened the Futong Canal, increasing annual grain transport by more than six hundred thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: He also dredged and widened the Futong Canal, adding more than six hundred thousand shi a year to the grain transport.

sentences.zh: 奉命括兩淮屯田，得疾，歸鎮江而卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: Ordered to survey military colonies in the two Huai regions, he fell ill, returned to Zhenjiang and died, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: While surveying military colonies in the two Huai regions he fell ill, returned to Zhenjiang, and died at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 子坤載。

translations.literal: His son was Kunzai.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kunzai succeeded him.

sentences.zh: ○劉恩

translations.literal: ○ Liu En
translations.idiomatic: Liu En

sentences.zh: 劉恩，字仁甫，洺之洺水人，後徙威州。

translations.literal: Liu En, style name Renfu, was a man of Moshui in Mo Prefecture; he later moved to Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu En, styled Renfu, was from Moshui in Mo Prefecture and later moved to Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 父辛，歸國，署貝州長。

translations.literal: His father Xin submitted to the state and was appointed chief of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xin submitted to the Yuan and was made chief of Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 恩幼知讀書，勇而有謀，以材武隸軍籍，累功為百戶，俄遷管軍總管，佩銀符，太傅府經歷。

translations.literal: En from youth knew how to read; he was brave and resourceful; for martial talent he entered military registers; through accumulated merit he became a hundred-household; soon he was transferred to army commander, wore the silver tally, and served as staff officer in the Grand Tutor's office.
translations.idiomatic: En learned to read as a boy and was both brave and shrewd. Listed for his martial skill, he rose through merit to hundred-household, then soon to army commander with a silver tally, serving on the staff of the grand tutor's office.

sentences.zh: 從入蜀，數有戰功。

translations.literal: He followed on the entry into Shu and had military achievements on several occasions.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaign into Sichuan and won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 宋劉整將兵守瀘州，中統三年都元帥紐璘遣恩諭整降，以功易賜金符。

translations.literal: The Song general Liu Zheng led troops to guard Luzhou; in the third year of Zhongtong Grand Marshal Niuchan sent En to persuade Zheng to surrender; for merit his tally was exchanged for a gold one.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song general Liu Zheng held Luzhou, Grand Marshal Niuchan sent En in the third year of Zhongtong (1262) to negotiate his surrender. For this service En's silver tally was exchanged for a gold one.

sentences.zh: 至元三年，宋將以戰船五百艘，載甲士三萬人，夾江上游，先以一萬人據云頂山，欲取漢州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhiyuan, a Song general with five hundred warships carrying thirty thousand armored troops moved upstream along both banks of the river; first ten thousand men occupied Yunding Mountain, intending to take Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhiyuan (1266) a Song commander brought five hundred warships and thirty thousand armored troops upstream along both banks of the river. Ten thousand men seized Yunding Mountain first, aiming to take Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 恩率千人渡江與戰，殺其將二人、士卒三千餘人，溺死者不可勝計，授成都路管軍副萬戶。

translations.literal: En led a thousand men across the river to fight, killed two of their generals and more than three thousand soldiers; those who drowned were beyond counting; he was appointed Deputy Ten-thousand-household of the Chengdu Route Army.
translations.idiomatic: En led a thousand men across the river, killed two Song generals and more than three thousand troops, and drowned so many that the dead were beyond counting. He was made deputy ten-thousand-household of the Chengdu route army.

sentences.zh: 六年，從平章賽典赤攻嘉定，過九頂山，與宋軍遇，生擒其部將十八人，械送京師，賞賚甚厚。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he followed Pingzhang Saidianchi in attacking Jiading; passing Jiuding Mountain, they met Song troops; he captured alive eighteen of their subordinate generals, sent them in fetters to the capital, and received very generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he followed Pingzhang Saidianchi against Jiading. At Jiuding Mountain they met Song forces; En took eighteen subordinate generals alive and sent them in chains to the capital, earning lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 九年，從皇子西平王、行省也速帶兒徵建都，恩將游兵為先鋒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he followed Prince Xiping and Regional Secretariat Yesudai'er in campaigning against Jiandu; En led light troops as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he followed Prince Xiping and the regional secretariat head Yesudai'er against Jiandu, leading light troops as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 師次其地，一日三戰皆捷。

translations.literal: When the army halted in that region, in one day three battles were all victorious.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached the area, it fought three battles in a single day and won them all.

sentences.zh: 建都兵夜來犯圍，恩御之，死者千餘人。

translations.literal: Jiandu troops came by night to attack the encirclement; En repelled them; more than a thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Jiandu forces attacked the siege lines at night; En drove them off, leaving more than a thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 時師久駐，食且盡，恩畫策招諭沿江諸蠻，得糧三萬石、牛羊二萬頭，士氣益振。

translations.literal: At that time the army had long encamped and provisions were nearly exhausted; En devised a plan to summon and persuade the various barbarians along the river, obtaining thirty thousand shi of grain and twenty thousand head of cattle and sheep; army morale greatly revived.
translations.idiomatic: The army had been encamped so long that food was running out. En devised a plan to win over the river tribes, obtaining thirty thousand shi of grain and twenty thousand head of livestock, and morale soared.

sentences.zh: 建都因山為城，山有七巔，恩奪其五，斷其汲道。

translations.literal: Jiandu used the mountain as a city; the mountain had seven peaks; En seized five of them and cut off their water route.
translations.idiomatic: Jiandu had fortified the mountain, which had seven peaks. En took five of them and cut off their water supply.

sentences.zh: 建都窮蹙，乃降。

translations.literal: Jiandu, driven to extremity, then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Jiandu, cornered, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 入朝，升管軍萬戶，戍眉州。

translations.literal: He entered court; was promoted to army ten-thousand-household and garrisoned Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He went to court, was made army ten-thousand-household, and garrisoned Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 十二年，昝萬壽以嘉定降，恩移戍嘉定。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Zan Wanshou surrendered Jiading; En was transferred to garrison Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, when Zan Wanshou surrendered Jiading, En was moved to garrison there.

sentences.zh: 安西王遣使召恩至六盤山，問曰：「江南已平，四川未下奈何？」

translations.literal: The Prince of Anxi sent an envoy to summon En to Liupan Mountain and asked: "Jiangnan is already pacified—what is to be done about Sichuan not yet being taken?"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Anxi summoned En to Liupan Mountain and asked, "Jiangnan is pacified, but Sichuan still holds out. What can be done?"

sentences.zh: 恩曰：「若以重臣之不徇私者奉詔督責之，則半年可下矣。」

translations.literal: En said: "If a high minister who does not favor private interests is sent by edict to supervise and press them, then within half a year it can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: En replied, "If the court sends a senior minister who will not play favorites to supervise the campaign and hold commanders accountable, Sichuan can fall within half a year."

sentences.zh: 王即遣恩與府僚術兒赤乘傳以聞，帝以為然，命丞相不花等行樞密院於西川，授恩同僉院事。

translations.literal: The Prince immediately sent En together with the prefectural official Shuerchi to ride the relay posts and report; the Emperor thought it right, ordered the Chancellor Buhua and others to operate the Bureau of Military Affairs in West Sichuan, and appointed En Associate Director of the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Anxi at once dispatched Liu En and the prefectural officer Shuerchi by relay to lay the matter before the throne. The Emperor approved, ordered Chancellor Buhua and others to establish the Bureau of Military Affairs in West Sichuan, and appointed En its Associate Director.

sentences.zh: 十五年，重慶降，守將張萬走夔府，以兵固守，不花遣恩招之，萬以城降。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Chongqing surrendered; the defending general Zhang Wan fled to Kuifu and held firm with troops; Buhua sent En to summon him, and Wan surrendered with the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Chongqing submitted. The garrison commander Zhang Wan withdrew to Kuifu and held out with his troops. Buhua sent Liu En to summon him, and Zhang Wan surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 旬月之間，得其大小州邑六十四。

translations.literal: Within a month or so, they obtained sixty-four large and small prefectures and districts.
translations.idiomatic: Within the space of a month, they brought sixty-four prefectures and districts, great and small, under their control.

sentences.zh: 十六年，入朝，賞賚有加，授四川西道宣慰使，改副都元帥。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he entered court; rewards and gifts were increased; he was appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Western Circuit of Sichuan and changed to Vice Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he came to court, where he received lavish rewards and was appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Western Circuit of Sichuan, with his rank raised to Vice Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 率蒙古、漢軍萬人徵斡端，進都元帥，宣慰使如故，賜宿烈孫皮衣一、錦衣一，及弓刀諸物。

translations.literal: Leading ten thousand Mongol and Han troops to campaign against Woduan, he was promoted to Grand Marshal; his post as Pacification Commissioner remained as before; he was granted one sukelesun fur coat, one brocade robe, and bow, sword, and other items.
translations.idiomatic: At the head of ten thousand Mongol and Han troops he marched against Woduan and was promoted to Grand Marshal, retaining his post as Pacification Commissioner. He received a sukelesun fur coat, a brocade robe, and a bow, sword, and other gifts besides.

sentences.zh: 師次甘州，奉詔留屯田，得粟二萬餘石。

translations.literal: The army halted at Ganzhou; receiving an edict, he remained to conduct garrison farming and obtained more than twenty thousand shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Ganzhou, he was ordered by edict to remain and open garrison farms, from which he harvested more than twenty thousand shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 十八年，命恩進兵斡端，海都將玉論亦撒率兵萬人迎戰，遊騎先至，恩設伏以待，大敗之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, En was ordered to advance on Woduan; Kaidu general Yulun Yisa led ten thousand troops to meet battle; vanguard cavalry arrived first; En set an ambush and waited, and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Liu En was ordered to advance on Woduan. Kaidu general Yulun Yisa came out with ten thousand men to give battle. The scouting cavalry arrived first; En laid an ambush and waited, then routed them utterly.

sentences.zh: 海都又遣八把率眾三萬來侵，恩以眾寡不敵，成師而還。

translations.literal: Kaidu again sent Baba leading thirty thousand men to invade; En, finding his numbers too few to match the enemy, withdrew his army intact.
translations.idiomatic: Kaidu sent Baba at the head of thirty thousand men to invade again. Outnumbered, Liu En drew off his forces intact.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，僉行樞密院事，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, he served as Associate Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he held the post of Associate Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and there he died.

sentences.zh: 子德祿，襲成都管軍萬戶。

translations.literal: His son Delu inherited the post of Commander of the Ten Thousand Households overseeing troops at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Delu succeeded him as Commander of the Ten Thousand Households in charge of the Chengdu garrison.

sentences.zh: ○石高山

translations.literal: ○ Shi Gaoshan
translations.idiomatic: Shi Gaoshan

sentences.zh: 石高山，德興府人。

translations.literal: Shi Gaoshan was a man of Dexing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Gaoshan was a native of Dexing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父忽魯虎，以侍衛軍從太祖定中原，太宗賜以東昌、廣平四十餘戶，遂徙居廣平之洺水。

translations.literal: His father Huluhu, with the Personal Guard, followed the Taizu in pacifying the Central Plains; the Taizong granted him more than forty households in Dongchang and Guangping, and he moved to dwell at Luoshui in Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huluhu had served in the Personal Guard under Taizu when the Central Plains were brought to order. Taizong granted him more than forty households in Dongchang and Guangping, and the family settled at Luoshui in Guangping.

sentences.zh: 中統三年，高山因平章塔察兒入見世祖，因奏曰：「在昔太祖皇帝所集按察兒、孛羅、窟裡台、孛羅海拔都、闊闊不花五部探馬赤軍，金亡之後，散居牧地，多有入民籍者。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong, Gaoshan, following the Grand Councillor Tacharer, entered audience with Shizu and memorialized, saying: "In former times the Taizu Emperor gathered the five divisions of tamachi cavalry—Ajicher, Boluo, Kulutei, Boluohaibadu, and Kuokuohua. After the fall of Jin they were scattered across pasture lands, and many entered civilian registers.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhongtong, Gaoshan accompanied Grand Councillor Tacharer to audience with Shizu and addressed the throne: "In days past Taizu assembled the tamachi cavalry of five divisions—Ajicher, Boluo, Kulutei, Boluohaibadu, and Kuokuohua. After Jin fell they were scattered across the grazing lands, and many had been entered on civilian registers.

sentences.zh: 國家土宇未一，宜加招集，以備驅策。」

translations.literal: The realm territory is not yet united; they ought to be gathered anew to prepare for deployment and service.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is not yet fully united; they should be summoned and mustered again, to stand ready for the state call.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，曰：「聞卿此言，猶寐而覺。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and said: "To hear your words is like waking from sleep."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was greatly pleased and said, "Your words are like waking from a dream."

sentences.zh: 即命與諸路同招集之。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered that they be gathered together with the various circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He at once ordered that they be mustered jointly with the other circuits.

sentences.zh: 既籍其數，仍命高山佩銀符領之。

translations.literal: Once their numbers were registered, he also ordered Gaoshan to wear the silver tally and command them.
translations.idiomatic: When their rolls had been compiled, he further ordered Gaoshan to take the silver tally and command them.

sentences.zh: 四年，授管軍總管，鎮息州，軍令嚴肅，寇不敢窺。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Troops and garrisoned Xizhou; military orders were strict, and bandits did not dare to venture near.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made Commander-in-Chief of Troops and posted to Xizhou. Discipline in the army was severe, and raiders did not dare approach.

sentences.zh: 居四年，邊境晏然，賜金符以獎之。

translations.literal: After four years the borderlands were tranquil, and he was granted a gold tally as reward.
translations.idiomatic: Four years passed in peace along the frontier, and he was rewarded with a gold tally of command.

sentences.zh: 至元八年，從取光州，克棗陽，進攻襄樊，皆有功。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan, he followed in the capture of Guangzhou, took Zaoyang, and advanced to attack Xiangyang and Fancheng; at all of these he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan he took part in the seizure of Guangzhou, the reduction of Zaoyang, and the assault on Xiangyang and Fancheng, distinguishing himself at each.

sentences.zh: 十年，從阿術略地淮上。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he followed Azhu in raiding the lands along the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he followed Azhu in sweeping the Huai region.

sentences.zh: 十一年，從下江南，以功升顯武將軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he followed in the reduction of Jiangnan and was promoted to General of Manifest Martiality for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he joined the conquest of Jiangnan and, for his service, was promoted to General of Manifest Martiality.

sentences.zh: 十二年冬，丞相伯顏命以所部兵取寧國，下令無虜掠。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twelfth year, the Chancellor Bayan ordered him to take Ningguo with his own troops, issuing an order forbidding seizure and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the twelfth year Chancellor Bayan ordered him to reduce Ningguo with his own command and strictly forbade looting.

sentences.zh: 既至城下，喻以禍福，寧國開門迎降，秋毫無犯。

translations.literal: When he reached the city walls, he explained blessings and calamities; Ningguo opened its gates to welcome surrender, and not a hair was harmed.
translations.idiomatic: When he came beneath the walls he set forth the rewards of submission and the cost of resistance. Ningguo opened its gates in welcome, and not the slightest harm was done.

sentences.zh: 復令兵從至焦山，與宋將孫虎臣、張世傑轉戰百餘里，殺獲甚多，以功賜金虎符，進信武將軍，鎮高郵。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to lead his troops to Jiaoshan; with the Song generals Sun Huchen and Zhang Shijie he fought a running battle of more than a hundred li, killing and capturing many; for his merit he was granted a gold tiger tally, promoted to General of Trustworthy Martiality, and stationed at Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered next to Jiaoshan, where he fought a running battle of more than a hundred li against the Song generals Sun Huchen and Zhang Shijie, slaying and capturing a great number. For this he received a gold tiger tally, was raised to General of Trustworthy Martiality, and garrisoned Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 宋平，伯顏等朝京師，帝問：「有瘦而善戰者，朕忘其名。」

translations.literal: When the Song was pacified, Bayan and others attended court at the capital; the Emperor asked: "There is one who is lean and skilled in battle—I have forgotten his name."
translations.idiomatic: After the Song realm was pacified, Bayan and the others came to court. The Emperor asked, "There was a lean man, fierce in battle—I have forgotten his name."

sentences.zh: 伯顏以高山對，且盛稱其功。

translations.literal: Bayan answered with Gaoshan and greatly praised his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan named Gaoshan and spoke at length of his deeds.

sentences.zh: 帝即召見，命高山自擇一大郡以佚老，而以所部軍俾其子領之，高山辭曰：「臣筋力尚壯，猶能為國驅馳，豈敢為自安計。」

translations.literal: The Emperor immediately summoned him and ordered Gaoshan to choose a large prefecture in which to retire in ease, while letting his son command his troops; Gaoshan declined, saying: "Your subject sinews and strength are still robust; I can still serve the state in campaign—how dare I seek my own comfort."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned him at once and bade Gaoshan choose any great prefecture where he might live out his years in ease, entrusting his command to his son. Gaoshan declined: "My strength is not yet spent, and I am still fit to ride for the realm. How could I think only of my own ease?"

sentences.zh: 帝從之，進顯武將軍，領兵北征，屯亦脫山。

translations.literal: The Emperor acceded, promoted him to General of Manifest Martiality, and had him lead troops on the northern campaign, encamping at Yituo Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor yielded to his wish, promoted him again to General of Manifest Martiality, and sent him north at the head of an army, where he encamped at Yituo Mountain.

sentences.zh: 十六年，命同忽都魯領三衛軍戍和林，因屯田以給軍儲，歲不乏用。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he was ordered together with Hudul to lead the Three Guards in garrisoning Karakorum; they undertook garrison farming to supply military stores, and year by year provisions never fell short.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he and Hudul were ordered to garrison Karakorum at the head of the Three Guards. They opened farms to feed the army, and in no year did supplies run short.

sentences.zh: 乃顏叛，督戰有功，賜三珠虎符、蒙古侍衛親軍都指揮使，守衛東宮。

translations.literal: When Nayan rebelled, he supervised battles to merit; he was granted a three-pearl tiger tally and made Commander-in-Chief of the Mongol Personal Guard, guarding the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Nayan rose in rebellion, he directed the fighting to good effect and was rewarded with a three-pearl tiger tally and the post of Commander-in-Chief of the Mongol Personal Guard, charged with guarding the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 成宗憫其老，以其子闊闊不花襲職，賜鈔三百錠。

translations.literal: Emperor Chengzong, pitying his age, had his son Kuokuohua succeed to the post and granted three hundred ding of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Chengzong, taking pity on his years, had his son Kuokuohua succeed to the command and granted three hundred ding in paper notes.

sentences.zh: 大德七年，卒於家，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dade, he died at home, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Dade he died at home, in his seventy-sixth year.

sentences.zh: ○鞏彥暉

translations.literal: ○ Gong Yanhui
translations.idiomatic: Gong Yanhui

sentences.zh: 鞏彥暉，易州人，與兄彥榮俱以武勇稱。

translations.literal: Gong Yanhui was a man of Yizhou; he and his elder brother Yanrong were both renowned for martial valor.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Yanhui was a native of Yizhou. He and his elder brother Yanrong were both famed for courage in battle.

sentences.zh: 初，彥榮經百夫長隸千戶何伯祥麾下，累有戰功，後告老，以彥暉代之。

translations.literal: At first Yanrong, having risen through centurion, served under the chiliarch He Boxiang; he repeatedly had battle merit; later he retired, and Yanhui replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: At first Yanrong, after serving as a centurion, fell under the command of the chiliarch He Boxiang and won repeated distinction in battle. When he retired in old age, Yanhui took his place.

sentences.zh: 諸軍伐宋，彥暉從破棗陽，斬首甚眾。

translations.literal: When the various armies campaigned against the Song, Yanhui followed in the capture of Zaoyang and beheaded very many.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against the Song, Yanhui took part in the fall of Zaoyang and claimed a great many heads.

sentences.zh: 萬戶張柔之駐曹武也，彥暉與伯祥別將一軍破大洪諸寨。

translations.literal: When the chiliarch Zhang Rou was encamped at Caowu, Yanhui and Boxiang separately commanded an army and broke the stockades at Dahong and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: While the chiliarch Zhang Rou held Caowu, Yanhui and He Boxiang led a separate force and overran the stockades at Dahong and the rest.

sentences.zh: 宋人出荊、鄂，選兵二萬救之。

translations.literal: The Song sent troops out from Jing and E, selecting twenty thousand men to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: The Song marched out of Jing and E with twenty thousand picked troops to relieve the place.

sentences.zh: 彥暉與伯祥逆戰，斬首五百級，生擒曹路分等一十六人。

translations.literal: Yanhui and Boxiang met them in battle, beheading five hundred, and capturing alive sixteen including Cao Lufen and others.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui and He Boxiang met them in battle, took five hundred heads, and captured sixteen men alive, among them Cao Lufen.

sentences.zh: 是夜，宋兵來攻，彥暉率甲士三十人，追擊於曹武鎮，敵潰走，擒其主將以歸。

translations.literal: That night the Song army came to attack; Yanhui led thirty armored soldiers in pursuit at Caowu Town; the enemy broke and fled; he captured their commander and returned.
translations.idiomatic: That night the Song force attacked again. Yanhui led thirty armored men in pursuit at Caowu Town, broke the enemy, and brought back their commander as a captive.

sentences.zh: 戰光州，柔軍於東北，夜二鼓，命彥暉率勁卒二百伏西南，五鼓，東北聲振天地，彥暉植梯先登，眾繼之，破其外城，遂急攻，併其子城破之。

translations.literal: At the battle of Guangzhou, Rou army was in the northeast; at the second watch of the night he ordered Yanhui to lead two hundred picked troops in ambush to the southwest; at the fifth watch noise shook heaven and earth in the northeast; Yanhui planted ladders and scaled first, the rest following; they broke the outer wall, then pressed the attack and together breached the inner citadel.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangzhou, Zhang Rou force lay to the northeast. At the second watch he sent Yanhui with two hundred picked men to lie in wait on the southwest. At the fifth watch a thunderous assault rose in the northeast; Yanhui set his ladders and climbed first, his men after him. They broke the outer wall, pressed hard, and took the inner citadel as well.

sentences.zh: 戰滁州，彥暉率浮渾脫者十人，夜渡池水，入欄馬牆，殺守軍三鋪，焚其東南角排寨木帘，大軍繼之，比明拔其城。

translations.literal: At the battle of Chuzhou, Yanhui led ten strong swimmers; crossing the moat water by night, they entered the horse-corral wall, killed the garrison at three outposts, burned the wooden palisade at the southeast corner, the main army followed, and by dawn they took the city.
translations.idiomatic: At Chuzhou, Yanhui led ten strong swimmers who crossed the moat by night, entered through the horse wall, and cut down the garrison at three outposts. They set fire to the wooden palisade on the southeast corner; the main force came up behind them, and by dawn the city had fallen.

sentences.zh: 會大軍攻黃州，諸將壁壘未定，有舟來覘，柔遣彥暉伏甲二百於赤壁之下。

translations.literal: When the main army attacked Huangzhou, the generals encampments were not yet fixed; a boat came to reconnoiter; Rou sent Yanhui with two hundred armored men in ambush below Chibi.
translations.idiomatic: As the main army besieged Huangzhou, the generals camps were not yet settled when a boat came to spy out their positions. Zhang Rou sent Yanhui with two hundred armored men to lie in wait below Chibi.

sentences.zh: 敵軍夜半果水陸並至，彥暉等曳槍俟其半過而擊之，敵大撓，死者無算，生擒十七人。

translations.literal: The enemy forces at midnight indeed arrived by water and land together; Yanhui and the others dragged their spears, waited until half had passed, then struck; the enemy was greatly routed, the dead beyond counting, seventeen captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight the enemy came by land and water together. Yanhui and his men held their spears low, let half the force pass, then struck. The enemy broke in disorder; the slain were beyond count, and seventeen were taken alive.

sentences.zh: 師還，又破張家寨，以守將獻。

translations.literal: The army returned, again broke Zhang Family Stockade, and presented the defending commander.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he stormed Zhang Family Stockade as well and sent up its commander as a captive.

sentences.zh: 從攻壽州，奪其門，生擒三人以出。

translations.literal: Following the attack on Shouzhou, he seized its gate and captured three alive and brought them out.
translations.idiomatic: At the assault on Shouzhou he forced the gate, took three men alive, and brought them out.

sentences.zh: 泗州之役，諸將自四鼓集城下，為塹水所阻，黎明無敢渡者，兩軍交射如雨。

translations.literal: At the battle of Sizhou, the generals from the fourth watch assembled below the city, were blocked by moat water, at dawn none dared cross, and the two armies exchanged volleys like rain.
translations.idiomatic: At Sizhou the generals gathered beneath the walls from the fourth watch onward, but the flooded moat held them back. At dawn none would cross, and the two sides exchanged arrows thick as rain.

sentences.zh: 彥暉被重甲徑渡，敵將來禦，彥暉刺其胸搏殺之。

translations.literal: Yanhui donned heavy armor and waded straight across; an enemy general came to meet him; Yanhui stabbed him in the chest and killed him in close combat.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui put on heavy armor and waded straight through the water. An enemy general came to block his path; Yanhui drove his blade into the man chest and killed him hand to hand.

sentences.zh: 眾畢渡，至晡得其外城，尋登其月城。

translations.literal: When the host had all crossed, by the bu hour they took its outer wall; soon after they ascended its moon fort.
translations.idiomatic: Once everyone had crossed, they took the outer wall by late afternoon and soon after scaled the barbican.

sentences.zh: 彥暉將下，顧​​伯祥失所在，乃與王進反求之。

translations.literal: Yanhui was about to descend; he turned and saw Boxiang was nowhere to be found, so he and Wang Jin went back to search for him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui was about to come down when he noticed Boxiang was missing. He and Wang Jin turned back to find him.

sentences.zh: 敵复追襲，彥暉力戰，翼伯祥以出，由是伯祥與彥暉如親昆弟然。

translations.literal: The enemy again pursued and attacked; Yanhui fought hard and shielded Boxiang out; from this Boxiang and Yanhui were like close brothers.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy gave chase again. Yanhui fought fiercely and fought his way out with Boxiang at his side. After that, Boxiang and Yanhui were as close as brothers.

sentences.zh: 事聞，賜彥暉銀符牌，俾兼鎮撫事。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Yanhui was granted a silver tally plaque and ordered concurrently to handle pacification affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Yanhui was awarded a silver tally and given concurrent charge of pacification duties.

sentences.zh: 歲己未十一月，兵渡江，次武昌。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the jiwei year, the army crossed the Yangtze and halted at Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the jiwei year the army crossed the Yangtze and encamped at Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 宋援兵四集，彥暉逆戰，有舟數十來挑戰，彥暉逐之入湖中，伏出，圍彥暉數匝，左右莫能近。

translations.literal: Song relief troops gathered from four directions; Yanhui met them in battle. Several dozen boats came to challenge; Yanhui chased them into the lake; ambushers emerged and surrounded Yanhui layer upon layer, and those at his sides could not approach.
translations.idiomatic: Song reinforcements converged from all sides and Yanhui met them in battle. Several dozen enemy boats came out to challenge him; he drove them into the lake, but hidden troops rose up and ringed him round and round until no one on his flanks could get near.

sentences.zh: 彥暉矢盡，短兵接，身被重傷，度不可免，遂投水中。

translations.literal: Yanhui exhausted his arrows and closed to short weapons; his body suffered grave wounds; judging that he could not escape, he threw himself into the water.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui ran out of arrows and fought hand to hand. Badly wounded and seeing no way out, he leapt into the water.

sentences.zh: 敵援之出，載歸江州，見宋官不屈，問以事不對，竟死，年五十六。

translations.literal: The enemy pulled him out, carried him back to Jiangzhou; facing Song officials he would not submit; questioned about affairs he answered not; in the end he died, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fished him out and brought him to Jiangzhou. He refused to bow before the Song officials and would answer none of their questions. He died at fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 長子信，襲授銀符，易州等處管軍總把。

translations.literal: His eldest son Xin inherited the post, was granted the silver tally, and became commander-in-chief of army management for Yizhou and other places.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Xin inherited the post, received the silver tally, and was made commander-in-chief of the garrison forces at Yizhou and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 中統三年，從征李璮。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong, he followed the campaign against Li Tan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhongtong he took part in the campaign against Li Tan.

sentences.zh: 至元四年，從元帥阿術南征。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiyuan, he followed Marshal A Shu on the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhiyuan he followed Marshal A Shu south on campaign.

sentences.zh: 九年，從攻樊城，先登，奪其土城，焚西南角樓，殺敵軍十人，擒五人。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he followed the attack on Fancheng, was first to ascend, took its earthen wall, burned the southwest corner tower, killed ten enemy soldiers, and captured five.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he joined the assault on Fancheng, was first over the wall, seized the earthen rampart, burned the southwest corner tower, killed ten of the enemy, and took five prisoners.

sentences.zh: 宋將矮張以舟兵來援，自高頭堡戰鬥八十餘里，抵襄陽城下，奪戰艦二，獲其裨將二人、軍八人。

translations.literal: Song general Ai Zhang brought naval forces to relieve the city; from Gaotou Fort he fought for more than eighty li and reached beneath Xiangyang walls; he captured two warships and took two enemy deputy generals and eight soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song general Ai Zhang came upriver with a fleet to relieve the city, Xin fought him from Gaotou Fort for more than eighty li all the way to the foot of Xiangyang walls, captured two warships, and took two deputy commanders and eight soldiers.

sentences.zh: 十一年，從丞相伯顏攻沙陽堡，率勇士五十，縱火焚其寨，敵軍大亂，遂破之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he followed Chancellor Bayan in attacking Shayang Fort, led fifty brave men to set fire and burn their stockade; the enemy army fell into great disorder and it was taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he followed Chancellor Bayan against Shayang Fort. Leading fifty picked men, he set fire to the enemy stockade; the garrison broke in panic and the fort fell.

sentences.zh: 是年，從渡江，與宋兵戰，俘生口十一，奪戰艦二。

translations.literal: That same year, he followed the crossing of the Yangtze, fought Song troops, took eleven captives, and captured two warships.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he crossed the Yangtze with the army, fought the Song forces, took eleven captives, and seized two warships.

sentences.zh: 繼又領軍由陸進，直抵鄂城下，殺宋兵數十人，擒江路分一人以歸。

translations.literal: He then led troops overland, went straight to the walls of Ezhou, killed several dozen Song soldiers, and brought back one Yangtze Route Commissioner captive.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his men overland straight to the walls of Ezhou, killed several dozen Song soldiers, and returned with a Yangtze Route Commissioner as prisoner.

sentences.zh: 十二年，戰丁家洲，殺宋兵七十餘人，奪戰艦二。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he fought at Dingjiazhou, killed more than seventy Song soldiers, and captured two warships.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he fought at Dingjiazhou, killed more than seventy Song soldiers, and captured two warships.

sentences.zh: 江南平，以功升武略將軍、管軍千戶，鎮太平州。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified, for his merit he was promoted to General of Martial Strategy and army thousand-household, garrisoning Taiping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the south was pacified, he was promoted for his service to martial-strategy general and army thousand-household and stationed at Taiping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以疾辭。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he resigned due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 子思明、思溫、思恭。

translations.literal: He had sons Siming, Siwen, and Sigong.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Siming, Siwen, and Sigong.

sentences.zh: 思明初患目疾，以思溫襲。

translations.literal: Siming at first suffered from eye disease, so Siwen inherited the post.
translations.idiomatic: Siming was stricken with an eye ailment at first, so Siwen inherited the post.

sentences.zh: 及思溫卒，而思明疾愈，復以思明襲。

translations.literal: When Siwen died and Siming illness had healed, Siming inherited again.
translations.idiomatic: After Siwen died and Siming recovered, Siming inherited the post once more.

sentences.zh: 思明卒，以思恭襲懷孟萬戶府管軍下千戶，佩金符。

translations.literal: When Siming died, Sigong inherited as sub-thousand-household of army management under the Huaimeng Ten-thousand-household Office, wearing the gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: When Siming died, Sigong inherited as sub-thousand-household of the Huaimeng ten-thousand-household garrison, with the gold tally.

sentences.zh: ○蔡珍

translations.literal: ○ Cai Zhen
translations.idiomatic: Cai Zhen

sentences.zh: ○張泰亨

translations.literal: ○ Zhang Taiheng
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Taiheng

sentences.zh: 張泰亨，堂邑縣人。

translations.literal: Zhang Taiheng was a native of Tangyi County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Taiheng was from Tangyi County.

sentences.zh: 父山，為管軍百戶。

translations.literal: His father Shan served as a hundred-household army commander.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shan had been a hundred-household army commander.

sentences.zh: 泰亨襲職，從攻宋釣魚山及樊城，徵女兒阿塔有功。

translations.literal: Taiheng inherited the post; he joined attacks on the Song positions at Mount Diaoyu and Fancheng and had merit in the campaign for Nuer Ata.
translations.idiomatic: Taiheng inherited the post and fought in the Song campaigns at Mount Diaoyu and Fancheng, distinguishing himself in the expedition for Nuer Ata.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，授銀符、侍衛軍總把。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong, he was granted the silver tally and made commander-in-chief of the Imperial Bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongtong he received the silver tally and was made commander-in-chief of the Imperial Bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 三年，從圍李璮有功。

translations.literal: In the third year, he had merit in the siege of Li Tan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he earned credit in the siege of Li Tan.

sentences.zh: 至元四年，賜金符，升京東歸德等處新軍千戶。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiyuan, he was given a gold tally and promoted to thousand-household of the newly raised forces in Jingdong, Guide, and other regions.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhiyuan he was awarded the gold tally and promoted to thousand-household of the newly raised forces in Jingdong, Guide, and neighboring districts.

sentences.zh: 從征西川有功，授元帥府鎮撫。

translations.literal: He had merit on the western Sichuan campaign and was appointed pacification commissioner of the marshal headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He served with distinction on the western Sichuan campaign and was made pacification commissioner of the marshal headquarters.

sentences.zh: 六年，改省都鎮撫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was transferred to provincial chief pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was reassigned as provincial chief pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 七年，從攻襄陽，矢中右臂。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he joined the attack on Xiangyang and was struck by an arrow in the right arm.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he joined the assault on Xiangyang and took an arrow in the right arm.

sentences.zh: 十年，從攻樊城。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he joined the attack on Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he took part in the attack on Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 十二年，進武略將軍、管軍總管，尋進明威將軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he was promoted to General of Martial Strategy and army commander-in-chief, and soon after to General of Bright Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was promoted to martial-strategy general and army commander-in-chief, and soon after to bright-martiality general.

sentences.zh: 從攻潭州，矢中鼻，拔矢奮戰，卻敵兵。

translations.literal: Joining the attack on Tanzhou, an arrow struck his nose; he pulled it out and fought on fiercely, repelling the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At the siege of Tanzhou an arrow struck his nose. He pulled it out, fought on with redoubled fury, and drove the enemy back.

sentences.zh: 十三年，賜虎符，進階武德。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was given a tiger tally and advanced in rank to Martial Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he received the tiger tally and was advanced in rank to Martial Virtue.

sentences.zh: 從征廣西，破靜江府。

translations.literal: He campaigned in Guangxi and took Jingjiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned in Guangxi and captured Jingjiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十四年，還軍潭州，金瘡發，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, returning with the army to Tanzhou, an old wound reopened and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, as the army was returning to Tanzhou, an old battle wound reopened and he died.

sentences.zh: 子繼祖襲，移鎮鄂州，舟過洞庭，溺死。

translations.literal: His son Jizu inherited the post; transferred to garrison Ezhou, his boat crossed Dongting Lake and he drowned.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jizu inherited the post and was transferred to garrison Ezhou, but drowned when his boat crossed Dongting Lake.

sentences.zh: 子震幼，以兄顯祖代之。

translations.literal: The son Zhen was young, so his elder brother Xianzu replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was still a boy, so his elder brother Xianzu took the post in his stead.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，從征交趾，陷沒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, he followed the campaign against Jiaozhi and was lost in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he joined the campaign against Jiaozhi and was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 震襲職，授金符、昭信校尉、管軍上千戶。

translations.literal: Zhen inherited the post, was granted the gold tally, made Defender-in-Chief of Manifest Faith, and commander of an upper thousand-household garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen inherited the post, received the gold tally, and was made defender-in-chief of manifest faith and commander of an upper thousand-household garrison.

sentences.zh: 延祐二年，覃恩加武略將軍，尋進階武德。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanyou, through a grace bestowal he was additionally made General of Martial Strategy, and soon advanced in rank to Martial Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yanyou a general amnesty raised him to martial-strategy general, and he was soon advanced in rank to Martial Virtue.

sentences.zh: 五年，升武節將軍、潁州萬戶府副萬戶。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was promoted to General of Martial Integrity and deputy ten-thousand-household of the Yingzhou Ten-thousand-household Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to martial-integrity general and deputy ten-thousand-household of the Yingzhou ten-thousand-household office.

sentences.zh: 天歷二年，卒，子珽襲。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianli, he died; his son Ting inherited.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianli he died, and his son Ting inherited.

sentences.zh: ○賀祉

translations.literal: ○ He Zhi
translations.idiomatic: He Zhi

sentences.zh: 賀祉，益都人。

translations.literal: He Zhi was a native of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhi was from Yidu.

sentences.zh: 父進，嘗平漣水有功，為元帥左監軍，守淄州；

translations.literal: His father Jin had once pacified Lianshui with merit, served as left military inspector under the marshal, and garrisoned Zizhou;
translations.idiomatic: His father Jin had once pacified Lianshui with distinction, served as the marshal left military inspector, and held garrison at Zizhou;

sentences.zh: 改千戶，守膠州。

translations.literal: Changed to commander of a thousand households; defended Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as commander of a thousand households and posted to defend Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 祉初以質子入宿衛，至元六年，襲父職為千戶，仍守膠州。

translations.literal: Zhi had first entered as a hostage to serve in the palace guard. In the sixth year of Zhiyuan, he inherited his father's office as commander of a thousand households and still defended Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had first come to the capital as a hostage in the imperial guard. In the sixth year of Zhiyuan he inherited his father's command as a thousand-household officer and continued to hold Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 七年，宋兵攻膠州，祉固守戰退之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Song troops attacked Jiaozhou. Zhi held firm, fought, and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Song forces besieged Jiaozhou. Zhi held the city through fierce fighting and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 十年，領舟師五百艘為先鋒，攻五河口城。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he led five hundred war vessels as vanguard to attack the city at Wuhekou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he led five hundred warships as the vanguard in the assault on the fortress at Wuhekou.

sentences.zh: 軍還，殿後。

translations.literal: When the army withdrew, he served as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: On the withdrawal he commanded the rearguard.

sentences.zh: 時宋兵以巨索橫截淮水，號混江龍，祉用大刀斷之，卻其救兵，清河城遂降。

translations.literal: At that time Song troops stretched great ropes across the Huai River to block it, calling the barrier Hunjianglong. Zhi cut it with a great blade, repelled their relief force, and Qinghe city then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Song had stretched massive chains across the Huai River—a barrier they called the River-Confounding Dragon. Zhi severed them with a great blade, turned back the relief force, and Qinghe surrendered.

sentences.zh: 攻高郵、寶應，戰淮安城下，屍填壕中。

translations.literal: He attacked Gaoyou and Baoying and fought below the walls of Huai'an; corpses filled the moat.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Gaoyou and Baoying, and beneath the walls of Huai'an the dead filled the moat.

sentences.zh: 丞相伯顏以其功上聞，授武節將軍。

translations.literal: Chancellor Bayan reported his achievements to the throne, and he was appointed General of Martial Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Bayan commended his achievements to the throne, and he was appointed General of Martial Integrity.

sentences.zh: 攻泗州，獲戰船五百艘還。

translations.literal: He attacked Sizhou, captured five hundred war vessels, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He took Sizhou, seized five hundred warships, and returned.

sentences.zh: 從右丞別乞裡迷失入朝，帝賜以弓矢、錦衣、鞍勒，加宣武將軍。

translations.literal: He followed the right chancellor Beglerbeg to court. The Emperor granted him bow and arrows, a brocade robe, and saddle fittings, and promoted him to General of Martial Proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the right chancellor Beglerbeg to court, where the Emperor granted him bow and arrows, a brocade robe, and saddle fittings, and promoted him to General of Martial Proclamation.

sentences.zh: 鎮新城，絕淮安、寶應糧道，降之，得戰船六百艘及器械。

translations.literal: He garrisoned Xincheng, cut off the grain routes of Huai'an and Baoying until they surrendered, and obtained six hundred war vessels and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: He garrisoned Xincheng, severed the grain routes to Huai'an and Baoying until both cities surrendered, and captured six hundred warships along with their armaments.

sentences.zh: 上於行樞密院，遂命領寶應軍民事。

translations.literal: The Emperor was then at the mobile Privy Council and ordered him to oversee the military and civilian affairs of Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was then at the mobile Privy Council and appointed him to administer both military and civil affairs in Baoying.

sentences.zh: 十四年，特賜金虎符、懷遠大將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was specially granted a golden tiger tally and the title Grand General Who Cherishes the Distant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was specially granted a golden tiger tally and the title Grand General Who Cherishes the Distant.

sentences.zh: 二十年，建寧路黃華反，以所領軍捕之，有功。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Huang Hua of Jianning Circuit rebelled. Leading the troops under his command, he captured him and earned merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, when Huang Hua rebelled in Jianning Circuit, he led his forces in pursuit and distinguished himself in the capture.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，以徵交趾請行，湖廣行省檄令守輜重，屯思明州。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he requested to go on the campaign against Jiaozhi. The Huguang Branch Secretariat ordered him to guard the baggage train and encamp at Siming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he volunteered for the campaign against Annam; the Huguang Branch Secretariat assigned him to guard the supply train, and he encamped at Siming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 軍還，至建康卒。
